description.value: A cross-sectional structural MRI study comparing regional cortical grey matter volumes in adult METH-dependent subjects and healthy non-METH users, examining age-related volume differences and drug-status-by-age interactions.

spans.text: The aim was to determine regional volumes of cortical grey matter in the brains of adult METH-users versus healthy control subjects, and their interaction with age and METH-usage variables.

description.value: Cross-sectional, non-randomized observational comparison of METH-dependent subjects and healthy non-METH user comparison subjects.

For each region, analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) was used to assess whether the effect of age on grey matter volume differed between METH-users and controls, using between-subject variables drug status (METH-user vs. control) and age (continuous), and the drug status by age effect.

definition.value: METH-users showed greater than normal age-related cortical grey matter loss compared to controls

spans.text: Among the six main lobes, the METH-users show greater than normal age-related cortical grey matter loss compared to control subjects in the frontal (ANCOVA interaction p=0.02), occipital (interaction p=0.01), and temporal (interaction p<0.001) cortices, and the insula (interaction p=0.01) ( Figure 2 ).

value: We found greater than normal age-related loss in cortical grey-matter volumes of the temporal, occipital, frontal, and insular lobes of a group of individuals with a history of METH-dependence compared to non-METH users.
